conventions.convention: Forcing order orientation: q ≤ p means q is stronger (weaker conditions above); incompatible means no common stronger condition; D dense means every p has q ≤ p in D; a filter is nonempty, upward closed and internally directed; no largest/weakest condition is required.
conventions.fixed_by: def-forcing-relation-for-atomic-formulas (restating the published conventions it invokes via def-dense-open-sets-and-model-generic-filters)

conventions.convention: Atomic clauses: equality is the conjunction of the two subset clauses and calls equality only on proper subnames; membership is the dense-witness clause; the side condition q ≤ p,s is vacuous when no such q exists, so a left empty name makes σ ⊆ τ vacuous while no condition forces membership in the empty name.

Formula forcing is a scheme over fixed finite formulas: p forces ¬ψ iff no q ≤ p forces ψ, and p forces ∃xψ iff the witness-forcing conditions are dense below p; no uniform truth predicate, no maximal-antichain selection, no AC.

Internal versus external forcing: ⊩^M is the internally defined predicate, and only the atomic relation is asserted absolute between a transitive ground model and the external recursion; quantified forcing relations need not agree across ground models.
Check names use every condition as coefficient (no top-only variant) and Ġ = {⟨p̌,p⟩ : p ∈ P}.

Hull conventions: only nonzero limit α; the least-witness default is the <_L-least element of L_α (available since ∅ ∈ L_α when α ≠ 0); the formula enumeration has a distinguished witness variable and allows unused parameters and k_i = 0; H_0 = A and H_{n+1} adds all f_i on tuples from H_n.
Levels and Def: L_0 = ∅, L_{α+1} = Def(L_α), L_λ = ⋃_{β<λ}L_β for nonzero limits; Def(∅) = {∅} by a separate clause; ρ_L(x) is the α with x first entering at α+1; L_α ∩ Ord = α.

Weak-level convention: no nonzero limit L-level is assumed to satisfy Infinity, Power Set, Replacement, a full Separation scheme or Choice; in particular L_ω = V_ω and does not satisfy Infinity, and claims about weak transitive sets must rest on the displayed finite certificates rather than internal ZF.

Cardinal successors: for an infinite cardinal κ, κ⁺ is the Hartogs successor ℵ(κ) (least ordinal not injectible into κ, hence least cardinal above κ) and no ambient Choice is used; all cardinal arithmetic in the GCH argument is computed inside L.
Diamond: the guesses satisfy A_α ⊆ α and the guessing set is stationary for every A ⊆ ω1 (stationary, not merely unbounded; A = ∅ and A = ω1 included); clubs need not contain 0 or ω1.

Failure-pair formulation of the diamond recursion: at each α the guess is the χ-least bad pair (B,D) with B ⊆ α, D ⊆ α club in α and S_ξ ≠ B∩ξ for all ξ ∈ D, the global failure pair is chosen χ-least under V=L, and badness is a bounded predicate in the fixed parameters.

Dense forcing equivalence: e: P → Q must preserve order, preserve and reflect compatibility and have dense image (injectivity and order reflection are not required); T translates coefficients by e(s), R by all p with e(p) ≤ q; round trips hold only modulo forced equality; Boolean zero is excluded before a completion is used as a forcing order.

Ordinal preservation is as sets only (Ord ∩ M[G] = Ord ∩ M, no claim on cardinals or cofinalities), and the countable-transitive-model theorem is conditional on an assumed externally countable CTM and never constructs one from consistency.

The uniform formal forcing verification is a hypothesis, not a consequence of the semantic forcing theorem: B must verify total primitive-recursive constructors from target refutations to ZFC proofs of finite-fragment source-model existence, conversion and soundness; effectiveness, standard-numeral correctness or an external CTM do not satisfy it.

False-statement discipline: external Con(ZFC) is required for the unprovability half of the CTM item, the stronger external Con(S) with S = ZFC + Con(ZFC) for its set-model counterexample, and external Con(ZF) for ZF ⊬ V=L; bare ZF cannot prove its own consistency.

load_bearing.statement: In ZF there are fixed formulas Enum, Decode, Hist and χ and a fixed finite sentence C with: Decode exactly for the definable subsets (separate empty-carrier branch giving Def(∅)={∅}); every nonzero limit L_λ satisfies C and, conversely, every nonempty transitive N satisfying C is L_β with β = N ∩ Ord; χ defines the actual <_L and its interpretation in every nonzero limit level agrees with that order.
In ZF, for a nonzero limit ordinal α, X ≺ (L_α,∈) and π: X → M the Mostowski collapse: M = L_β for β = M ∩ Ord, π fixes every transitive A ⊆ X pointwise, and π(ξ) is the order type of X ∩ ξ.

In ZF, for a nonzero limit α and A ⊆ L_α, H = Hull^{L_α}(A) exists and (H,∈) ≺ (L_α,∈); if A is infinite and well-orderable then H is well-orderable with |H| = |A|; if A is finite (including empty) then H is countably infinite.

Work in ZF with a nonempty forcing preorder P, q ≤ p meaning q is stronger: σ ⊆ τ by the common-extension clause, equality by both subset clauses, membership by the dense equality-witness clause; subset is auxiliary and no largest condition is required.

For each fixed finite formula forcing extends the atomic relations by conjunction, negation p ⊩ ¬ψ iff no q ≤ p forces ψ, and existential p ⊩ ∃xψ iff the witness-forcing set is dense below p; one predicate per formula, no AC and no maximal-antichain selection.

If p forces φ and q ≤ p then q forces φ; if {q : q forces φ} is dense below p then p forces φ; {q : q forces φ or q forces ¬φ} is dense in P; and an M-generic G containing p meets every ground dense-below-p set.
For a transitive ZF ground model M containing nonempty P and G M-generic: M[G] ⊨ φ(τ⃗_G) iff some p ∈ G forces φ(τ⃗) over M, for each fixed formula, with no ambient or ground-model AC.

Forcing is uniformly definable from P and the name parameters over a transitive ZF M for each fixed formula and satisfies the truth lemma; if generics through every condition are available, p forces φ over M iff M[G] ⊨ φ for every M-generic G containing p.

In ambient ZF, for transitive ZF M, nonempty P in M and M-generic G: M[G] is a transitive ZF model, M ⊆ M[G], G ∈ M[G]; if M satisfies AC then M[G] satisfies AC, the AC branch using ground-model Choice only.
In ambient ZF, Ord ∩ M[G] = Ord ∩ M; no preservation of cardinality or cofinality is asserted.
ZF proves L_α is well-orderable and |L_α| = |α| for every infinite ordinal α.
In ZF, if κ is an infinite cardinal and x ∈ L with x ⊆ κ then x ∈ L_{κ⁺}; more generally x ∈ L with x ⊆ L_κ gives x ∈ L_β for some β < κ⁺, where κ⁺ is the Hartogs successor.
ZF proves that L satisfies GCH; equivalently ZF proves V = L implies AC + GCH.
ZF proves V = L implies ◊ on ω1: for every A ⊆ ω1 the set of correct guesses is stationary, not merely unbounded.

For e: P → Q order-preserving, compatibility-preserving and -reflecting with dense image, the recursive translations T and R satisfy p forces φ(σ⃗) iff e(p) forces φ(Tσ⃗) for every fixed formula; every condition forces TR(τ) = τ and RT(σ) = σ; supplied generics correspond bijectively with M[G] = M[H].

In ambient ZF, given an externally countable transitive ZFC model M, nonempty P ∈ M and p ∈ P, some M-generic G contains p; the extension is externally countable, transitive, ZFC, has the same ordinals, and satisfies the truth lemma; no existence of a CTM is asserted.

Given a fixed finite target fragment Δ with a formal ZFC forcing verification for it, some fixed finite Γ ⊆ ZFC suffices for that verification and for the construction over a countable transitive Γ-model of a generic extension satisfying Δ.

If an arithmetic base B verifies total primitive-recursive constructors from certified T-refutations to ZFC proofs of finite-fragment source-model existence and conversion, plus the soundness constructor, then B ⊢ Con(ZFC) → Con(T).

concerns.concern: Step 3.1 asserts rather than derives that the Cohen construction 'has the uniform formal verification required by F5': it claims a PA-verified total primitive-recursive constructor from ZFC+¬(V=L) refutations to ZFC refutations, but only sketches the matrix-expansion blocks for target axioms and the extra tag, and it never names the reflection/source-fragment-existence constructor that the cited corollary (through lem-forcing-transfer-for-finite-zfc-fragments) also requires. The companion items thm-formal-consistency-transfer-by-forcing and cor-relative-consistency-from-a-forced-sentence deliberately carry this verification data as a hypothesis, so discharging it is this item's own burden. If the sketch is judged insufficient the refutation has no Con(ZFC+¬(V=L)) premise (the conclusion ZF ⊬ V=L is true but this route would be unproved). Note the Foundations bootstrapping boundary forbids importing the recorded not-proved-here Cohen page instead.

Items 3 and 4 of the statement (one fixed finite sentence C holds in every nonzero limit L-level and characterizes the nonempty transitive sets that are L-levels; the fixed χ agrees with <_L in every nonzero limit level) are the sole supplier for both condensation and the V=L → ◊ proof. The proof supports them with a bespoke formalization: an inventory of W-clauses summarized as 'the existence and exactness of the assignment and truth tables for every nonempty carrier', external inductions through accepted histories, and stage-counting for H_γ ∈ L_{γ+8}, R_γ ∈ L_{γ+32}, K_γ ∈ L_{γ+40}. I traced the strategy (external induction makes internal histories actual; limit prefixes are bounded unions; the bounds have slack) and found no false step, but the exact clause list of W and the successor/limit stage arithmetic should be checked clause by clause. No consumer uses the numeric bounds quantitatively, so only a failure of the C/χ characterization would be fatal.

Two steps needed for the contradiction are compressed. (a) Step 3.1 'Elementarity makes X ∩ ω1 an ordinal' silently uses that X is downward closed in ordinals: the reconstruction needs ω ⊆ X (empty set plus closure under the successor formulas) and, for ξ ∈ X ∩ ω1, a surjection ω → ξ inside X so that every η < ξ is f(n) with n ∈ X. (b) Step 5.1 'any preceding pair would belong to M' needs M = L_γ to be an initial segment of the χ-order (cited from the finite-stage lemma) together with absoluteness of the bounded badness predicate between the transitive M and the universe; the text states these facts only in passing. Both reconstructions go through, but a Step-7 reader must supply them.

The definition says 'Fix an enumeration (φ_i) of all membership formulas with a distinguished witness variable' and then concludes that 'the enumeration, default and least-witness rule are fixed; no family of arbitrary choices is implicit'. The hull is canonical only relative to that fixed enumeration: the definition never ties it to the published definable syntax coding (def-set-coded-terms-and-formulas / lem-canonical-well-order-of-finite-definition-codes), so as written it hides one parameter. Elementarity and the size claims are enumeration-independent and consumers only need some hull with the stated properties, so this is wording-level; the title and the no-choice wording overstate what is literally defined.

The statement asserts that for the fixed certified presentations the axiom and proof translators can be chosen primitive recursive and that PA verifies their totality and checker acceptance, and step 2.1 fixes the eight constant blocks (six ZF axiom tags plus the selected AC and GCH sentences). The proof argues the dispatcher's correctness by induction on the formula/line schedule but never exhibits those fixed derivations; the AC and GCH blocks in particular run through the condensation-side machinery. The underlying Gödel-style L-interpretation is standard and the item is explicit that the claim concerns fixed presentations, so this is a bookkeeping (not plausibility) burden: a Step-7 check should confirm that no uniform internal all-fragment assertion is being smuggled in and that the constant blocks are indeed finite.
